question: The Formosan leftovers of the gap audit of 26 November 2026 (Lin 2022 Tables 4.3-4.38, 7.1-7.5; Shibata 2020 Table 5.6; Tseng 2023 Tables 3.2.x, 4.2.x, 6.4; Yeh 2024 Tables 4.3-4.25, 6.14-6.15; Goderich 2020 Tables 4.42-4.45, 4.50; Shibata 2025 Tables 3.14, 3.16, 3.29, 3.31, 6.15-6.31; Chuang 2024 Table 6.1): what is entered?
chosen_reading: Two sporadic rows from Yeh (2024: 210): Katripulr *-s > -t in 'to catch' and Kasavakan *ɖ (here *ʐ) > h in 'mountain'. Nothing else. Lin's Tables 4.3-4.23 illustrate dialect reflexes that the rows of his chapter 6 and the stated-unchanged inheritance of the ten dialects already give; his consonant harmony (Tables 4.31-4.38) is word by word, 'the directionality and the environment ... seems random' (p. 97); Tables 7.1-7.5 list regular and irregular reflexes of PAN *d, the irregular ones being loans, contamination or doubtful PAN etyma. Shibata (2020) Table 5.6 is a list of seven irregular words. Goderich's Table 4.50 is the list of changes already entered on the Atayal nodes and dialects; Tables 4.42-4.44 are its examples. Shibata (2025) Tables 3.14-3.31 reproduce the reconstructions of Tseng, Lin, Yeh and Chuang, entered from those works, and Tables 6.15-6.31 restate the reflexes in his own PAn values, which are the notation system 'Shibata'. Chuang's Table 6.1 has the Proto-Paiwan reflexes already entered from his chapter 4, beside Li's (1977) Proto-Rukai and Ting's (1978) Proto-Puyuma.
alternatives: Enter the lexical irregularities as sporadic rows: Lin's PAN *d > PAS *t in *duSa, *qaRidaŋ, *kudəm and *d > *k in *dapa, *dəRuŋ (pp. 147-150), and his harmony forms dialect by dialect. Enter Tseng's Table 6.4 (Taokas and Saisiyat reflexes of six PAN phonemes after Ross 2012: 1274-1275) with Ross (2012), the next source of the audit; Taokas is not a lect. Enter Shibata's (2025) notes on phonetic paths (Table 6.15: PAn *S > Proto-Atayal s, 'sporadically [ʃ]') as allophones.
